secret.note: Copy it now and keep it somewhere safe: it won't be shown again. If you lose it, create another one.

endpoint.vehicles: Vehicles, with their last position, odometer and engine hours
endpoint.events: Events and alerts; with “after” you get only the new ones
endpoint.modules: Data from the modules the account has
endpoint.dispatch: Create a dispatch (key that can write)
endpoint.fill: Log a fill-up (key that can write)

keys.title: API keys
keys.note: Each system that queries your account gets its own: that way you can remove one without touching the others
keys.empty: No keys yet. Create one so your accounting system, your CRM or a tool like n8n or Make can query your vehicles.

usage.title: How to use it
usage.note: Each key allows {{n}} requests per minute
usage.lead: Each request carries the key in a header. For example, to get the vehicles with their position:
usage.openapiNote: Postman, n8n, Make and code generators read that file and build the requests on their own.

remove.title: Remove key
remove.body: The key “{{name}}” stops working right away. The system using it won't be able to query your account until you give it another one.

dialog.title: New API key
dialog.name: Which system it's for
dialog.canWriteNote: Create dispatches and log fill-ups. Unchecked, the key can only read.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.note: When something happens in your account, the address you give is notified right away
webhooks.secretNote: Every notification is signed with it. Your system uses it to check that the notification comes from us and not from someone else.
webhooks.empty: No webhooks yet. They let another system receive your alerts without having to ask: an ERP, a CRM, or a tool like n8n, Make or Zapier.

payload.title: What your system receives
payload.note: A POST with the event as JSON and a signature
payload.delivery: If your system answers with a 2xx code, the notification counts as delivered. If not, it's retried after a minute, after 5 and 30 minutes, and after 2 and 6 hours. Each delivery carries the headers <h>X-OpenGPS-Event</h>, <h>X-OpenGPS-Timestamp</h> and <h>X-OpenGPS-Signature</h>.
payload.verify: How your system checks the notification comes from us (Node.js)

sample.label: Speeding
sample.summary: was going 112 km/h with a 90 km/h limit

dialog.urlHint: The one the other system gives you to receive notifications.
dialog.headers: Custom headers <note>· optional: the key the other system asks for</note>
dialog.headersReplace: When you save, these replace the previous ones.
dialog.logEmpty: Nothing has been sent to it yet.
dialog.confirmDelete: The webhook is deleted with its log. It will stop receiving notifications.
dialog.needEvents: Choose at least one event, or mark that it wants all of them.
dialog.badHeader: Each header needs its name (letters, numbers and hyphens) and its value.

automations.title: Automations
automations.note: When this happens, on these vehicles and at these times, do this
automations.empty: No automations yet. For example: when an engine fault code appears, open a work order; or when a truck enters a forbidden zone at night, email the supervisor.

dialog.when: 1 · When any of these events happens
dialog.groupOption: Those in a group, with its subgroups
dialog.timed: Only on certain days and times
dialog.overnight: Goes past midnight: ends the next day.
dialog.addressesHint: Up to five, separated by commas. The channel must be connected on the platform.
dialog.customHint: Up to five emails or phones, separated by commas: each one fills the variables of whoever receives it in Custom. If empty, it is sent once.
dialog.noWebhooks: First create a webhook in its tab: here you choose which one is notified.
dialog.orderHint: Empty: the event's name. The order stays open, as corrective, in Maintenance.
dialog.cooldownHint: For the same vehicle. 0: acts every time.
dialog.needTrigger: Choose at least one event to trigger it.
dialog.cooldownRange: The wait goes from 0 to 1,440 minutes.
dialog.needAddresses: Enter one to five destinations, separated by commas.
dialog.needWebhook: First create a webhook in its tab.

sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.note: Temperature probes, doors, scales and other devices that send their readings over the internet
sensors.keyNote: The sensor, or the device that reads it, sends each reading like this:
sensors.emptyHint: Add one, set its range and, if it's on a vehicle, its out-of-range readings will show up as alerts for that vehicle.

dialog.noVehicle: None: it's at a fixed place
dialog.vehicleNote: If it's on a vehicle, when a reading leaves its range it becomes an alert for that vehicle, and it can trigger an automation.
dialog.notNumbers: The minimum and maximum must be numbers.
dialog.minBelowMax: The minimum must be less than the maximum.

chart.never: It hasn't sent any readings yet.
chart.label: Readings of {{name}}: from {{min}} to {{max}}
chart.limitNote: The dotted red line is the limit of the range.

export.title: Export
export.note: To open in Excel or move to another system

import.title: Import
import.note: From a CSV file: the first line holds the column titles
import.vehiclesNote: “model” is the GPS device's, as it appears when you add one. Each vehicle waits for the first report from its device.
import.geofencesNote: A circle has lat, lon and radius; a polygon, its points as “lat lon”, separated by semicolons.
import.existing: Anything that already exists is left as it is.
import.easiest: The easiest way: export first, fill in the file in the same format and save it as CSV.
import.noPermission: Importing data requires the permission to manage integrations.
